reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 discusses local stacking fault energy variations and nanotwin-mediated plasticity in CoCrFeNi nanopillars under quasi-static tension, not dynamic intermittent depinning. E2 addresses dislocation avalanches in SLM-processed materials under quasi-static compression, not the proposed high-strain-rate mechanism in single-phase CoCrFeMnNi. Neither passage provides evidence for spatially varying pinning sites from lattice distortions or the transition to burst-like dynamics at high strain rates.
premises: Severe lattice distortions in CoCrFeMnNi create spatially varying dislocation pinning sites
At high strain rates, dislocations undergo intermittent depinning and rapid re-pinning
This burst-like dislocation activity leads to enhanced dynamic hardening and ductility
Quasi-static deformation shows more homogeneous dislocation motion without pronounced bursts
